text:
Colorado nearly erased a three-goal deficit in the last four minutes. Artturi Lehkonen scored twice, the second with five seconds left, to pull COL within a goal, but New Jersey held on for a 4-3 win at Prudential Center. Jesper Boqvist's goal at 16:05 of the third had made it 4-1, and the rally began 42 seconds later.

Until the third period, the game belonged to the Devils. NJD led the first two periods in expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the number of shots, by 1.20 to 0.59 and 0.97 to 0.37. Luke Evangelista opened the scoring, and Declan Chisholm made it 2-1 on a shot with roughly a 1% chance of going in. Evangelista, named first star, added an assist and put six shots on goal. Arseny Gritsyuk's backhand early in the third made it 3-1. Then COL took over, out-chancing NJD 1.65 to 0.56 in the period, and the late goals followed. The game was close to even over 60 minutes: NJD deserved to win 51% of the time, meaning that share of simulated replays of every shot, against 49% for COL.

Both goalies finished slightly below expectation. Jake Allen stopped 31 of 34 shots for NJD, and Scott Wedgewood stopped 37 of 40 for COL. Neither team scored on its one power play. The facts provided don't include streaks or records, so there is nothing to say here about where the result leaves either club.
